Petitioner is engaged in the business of bottling of drinking water from the unit, which was established at Keezhmad within the limits of Keezhmad Grama Panchayath in the year 1999, which according to the the petitioner was done after obtaining necessary licence from the Panchayat.
It is also pointed out that, petitioner has obtained permission and no objection from various statutory authorities for running the unit.
The licence issued by the Panchayat was renewed from time to time, and finally by Ext.P8 from 01.04.2017 to 31.03.2018.
Since the licence was due to expire on 31.03.2018, petitioner submitted application for renewal of licence on 27.02.2018 and also remitted the necessary fee.

However, by Ext.P9, 3rd respondent intimated that, the licence can be renewed only on production of no objection certificate from the State Ground Water Authority an authority constituted under the Kerala State Ground Water (Control and Regulation)Act 2002.

sentences.text:
Therefore,
petitioner has submitted Ext.P11 application before the said authority, which is pending consideration.
According to the petitioner, in spite of earnest efforts of the petitioner, no steps are initiated, which necessitated in filing the writ petition.

2. A counter affidavit is filed by the 2nd and 3rd respondents, refuting the allegations, claims and demands raised by the petitioner and justifying the stand adopted in the communication issued by the Panchayat to the petitioner.

It is also pointed out that, whenever the petitioner is producing necessary NOC from the statutory authority, the D&O licence application submitted by the petitioner will be considered by the Panchayat.

sentences.text: 3. The 4th respondent has also filed a statement and among other submissions it is stated that the office has conducted a hydro geological investigation and pumping test in the borewell and based on the pumping test data, recommendations on the quantity of water that can be safely extracted from the borewell, for industrial use will be submitted in the forthcoming District Level Evaluation Committee for the extraction of ground water in the month of October 2018.

4. Today, when the matter is taken up, learned Government Pleader has produced a communication dated 12.11.2018 addressed by the District Officer of the Ground Water Department stating that,
already steps have been initiated and necessary recommendations have been made on 24.10.2018,
and within a reasonable time a final adjudication will be made.
It is also pointed out that, 20,000 litres per day is recommended.

5. Having heard respective counsel across the Bar and taking into account the pleadings of the respective parties, I am of the concerned opinion that, this writ petition can be disposed of with suitable directions.

The 5th respondent shall finalise the proceedings pertaining to the recommendation made by the District Authority dated 24.10.2018 at the earliest possible and at any rate, within 45 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
This writ petition is disposed of accordingly.

Sd/-
